title: Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic to be named AI national champions, WSJ reports
excerpt: The Trump administration plans to name more than two dozen AI national champions to help them sell abroad, days after Jensen Huang quit Nvidia.
content_html:
The Trump administration plans to name Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic among more than two dozen AI “national champions”, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday. The aim is to help US AI firms win business overseas against Chinese rivals.

People familiar with the plans told Yoko Kubota and Amrith Ramkumar that the announcement could come within the next week. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick would unveil the list of AI national champions, the Journal reported. The timing could still change.

A package deal for foreign buyers

The programme aims to persuade foreign governments and companies to choose US AI over Chinese technology. It would bundle American chips, AI models and other products into packages that are easier for overseas customers to buy, according to the Journal.

Commerce already runs the American AI Exports Program. A July 2025 executive order set it up to sell full packages of US AI abroad. In July this year, the department said groups of companies had filed 78 applications. Packages it designates may get government advocacy, federal financing and faster export licence reviews, it said.

China is pushing its own AI abroad too. In October, Chinese state media said Beijing had cleared DeepSeek and MiniMax to take their models overseas.

Nvidia under scrutiny

The plan shows the administration pressing ahead with its tech strategy despite the turmoil at Nvidia, the Journal reported. Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday. He had admitted an affair with Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect of spying for China.

The revelations have added to pressure from critics who want national security put ahead of market share, the Journal reported. Some fear Chinese companies are getting top Nvidia chips through gaps in export controls.

Trump has repeatedly praised Nvidia and Huang. In October he gave Huang the National Medal of Science.

Critics have accused Lutnick’s Commerce Department of failing to close those gaps, the Journal reported. It had previously reported that he was wary of angering Beijing during trade talks. Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Commerce “has the pen” on blacklisting Megaspeed. The Singapore firm sits at the centre of the Nvidia case.

The list would land in the week Trump travels to China. He attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on 18 and 19 November. He plans to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping there.
